questions.question: Your organization uses GitHub Copilot Business. You must ensure that developers never see Copilot suggestions that match code in public repositories. What should you configure?

options.text: Set Suggestions matching public code to Allow
options.why: Allow displays matching suggestions with code references. It does not hide them.

options.text: Add a content exclusion with the path "*"
options.why: Content exclusions apply to files in your repositories, not to matches with public code.

options.text: Set Suggestions matching public code to Block
options.why: Correct. Block prevents Copilot from showing suggestions that match public code.

options.text: Disable Copilot Chat in the IDE policy
options.why: Disabling chat does not affect inline suggestions or public code matching.

questions.explanation: The Suggestions matching public code policy set to Block hides suggestions that match public code.

questions.question: Developers want to see the license of public code that matches a Copilot suggestion so that they can decide whether to use it. Which configuration meets the requirement?

options.text: Set Suggestions matching public code to Allow so that code references are shown
options.why: Correct. With Allow, Copilot shows matching suggestions with code references that include the repository and license.

options.text: Set Suggestions matching public code to Block so that licenses are listed in the audit log
options.why: With Block, matching suggestions are hidden, and licenses are not listed in the audit log.

options.text: Enable the coding agent policy
options.why: The coding agent policy is unrelated to code references.

options.text: Add the license file to .github/copilot-instructions.md
options.why: Custom instructions do not produce code references.

questions.explanation: Code references, which list the matching repository and license, are shown when the policy is set to Allow.

questions.question: The public code policy is set to Allow. A developer accepts an inline suggestion in Visual Studio Code that matches public code. Where can the developer view the code reference details?

options.text: In the repository's Security tab under code scanning alerts
options.why: Code scanning alerts report vulnerabilities, not public code matches.

options.text: In the GitHub Copilot Log (Code References) channel of the Output panel
options.why: Correct. VS Code lists inline suggestion matches, with repository and license, in this Output channel.

options.text: In the organization's audit log
options.why: The audit log records administrative events, not individual code references.

options.text: In the pull request summary generated by Copilot
options.why: PR summaries describe changes. They do not list code references for inline suggestions.

questions.explanation: Inline code references appear in Output › GitHub Copilot Log (Code References). Chat lists references in the answer.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about the Suggestions matching public code setting are true? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: For developers with Copilot Business seats, the setting is controlled by the organization or enterprise.
options.why: Correct. Organization owners set the policy for their seats, and an enterprise can enforce it.

options.text: Each developer on Copilot Business can override the organization's setting in personal settings.
options.why: Developers with organization seats cannot override the organization's policy.

options.text: The filter applies to matches of about 150 characters or more.
options.why: Correct. Short, common code does not trigger the filter. Matches of about 150 characters or more do.

options.text: The filter applies to every line of code, including single keywords.
options.why: Short snippets do not trigger matching.

questions.explanation: The organization or enterprise controls the setting for business seats, and matching targets stretches of about 150 characters or more.

questions.question: An enterprise has 12 organizations. Security policy requires that all organizations block suggestions matching public code, and organization owners must not be able to change the setting. What should the enterprise owner do?

options.text: Select No policy for Suggestions matching public code
options.why: No policy lets each organization decide, which does not meet the requirement.

options.text: Ask each organization owner to set the policy to Block
options.why: Organization owners could change the setting later, so the requirement is not met.

options.text: Configure an enterprise content exclusion
options.why: Content exclusions apply to repository files, not public code matching.

options.text: Enforce the policy at the enterprise level with the value Blocked
options.why: Correct. An enforced enterprise policy applies to every organization, and organizations cannot override it.

questions.explanation: Enterprise owners can enforce a Copilot policy for all organizations, removing the choice from organization owners.
